output.title: Synthetic test data: use it to decide, not to stall
output.body:
Synthetic test data is useful when it helps you decide faster. It is not useful when it becomes a project of its own. For an owner-operator, the real question is simple: are you building test data because you need privacy or scale, or because nobody has tried the workflow on real records yet?

If the workflow is a repeatable one like invoice handling or customer inquiry triage, start smaller. Use a limited real-data subset, clear rules, and a human approval step wherever money or another high-risk decision is involved. That keeps the work focused on the process, not on polishing fake data until it looks convincing.

Bareni’s accounts-payable demo shows the boundary well. It uses entirely synthetic data to demonstrate the mechanics: text-based extraction, arithmetic checks, duplicate blocking, and audit records. But the demo’s limits matter too. The default route uses pre-extracted files, and PDF or scan ingestion plus OCR are not implemented. So it is useful for showing control logic, not for pretending it is ready for every invoice pile.

One practical next step: pick one workflow, one approval rule, and one small batch of real records. Then ask whether synthetic data is solving a real testing problem, or just delaying the moment you learn what the workflow actually needs.
